newsitem.title: Indonesia: Ten detained after gang war in Indonesian capital.
newsitem.headline: Ten detained after gang war in Indonesian capital.

text.p: Security forces detained at least 10 people after a turf war between two gangs in the central Jakarta district of Tanah Abang closed a busy market after a confrontation on Thursday, police said.

A policeman on duty in the shopping district near where the early morning clash took place said a number of people had been detained after gang war in which residents said men carrying samurai swords and daggers threw stones at each other.

"Ten people have been taken to the local military command for questioning," the policeman, who declined to give any further details, told reporters. Witnesses said they saw around 40 taken away in trucks.
Residents said soldiers who arrived at the scene as the fighting was taking place surrounded the combatants and forcefully dispersed onlookers. However, it was not clear how the fighting was stopped.
All but a few shops in the area had re-opened by the afternoon with troops and police still on guard and there was no sign of any damage to the buildings at the fight site.
News of the dispute spread quickly through Jakarta's financial markets, which have been jolted by recent riots and protests in Indonesia.
The fighting prompted shop owners in Tanah Abang quickly closed their stores as a precaution.
They said the two gangs, one consisting of ethnic East Timorese men and the other made up of ethnic Irianese, were fighting for territorial control of the district.
Tanah Abang, an important area for the textile trade in Jakarta and home to a number of local banks, is also known for its cheap accommodation and its red-light district.
